verdicts.reason: The need is documented. Reliability gates HfO2 and IGZO memories: the 1Mb HZO array at IEDM 2023 holds 1-month retention at 85C, and imec's 2T0C PBTI lifetime is ~1 yr against a 5-yr target. FMC itself relies on an outside test partner (Neumonda). My search found no U.S. commercial contract lab for ferroelectric or oxide-memory reliability; Radiant Technologies (Albuquerque) sells testers, and no Radiant contract-testing service turned up (snippet). So the gap is plausible but STILL-UNVERIFIED. The card is optimistic on demand and margin. Radiant RT66B-class testers that run hysteresis, PUND, fatigue, retention and imprint already sit in university shared facilities, so only wafer-level statistics, JEDEC-style qualification and radiation coordination are worth outsourcing, and the U.S. pool for that is perhaps 10-30 customers [ESTIMATE].

verdicts.reason: The card's only axis is supply security, and an unqualified U.S. startup improves it for none of the named buyers. Target incumbents are already non-Chinese: Materion holds IGZO-target patents via its ex-Heraeus unit (US9051646, snippet), and Japanese makers lead display IGZO. Research-grade IGZO targets already sell from the U.S. (American Elements, snippet), and the real chokepoint, primary gallium and indium refining, sits upstream of any target or precursor maker. Demand is soft too. Samsung's IGZO channel is only 'reported' (TrendForce 2026-04), and an Oct-2026 report says there is no fixed mass-production timetable. Micron, the only U.S. DRAM maker, is reported to be skipping 4F2 (snippets), so there is no onshore volume customer. Vertical-channel and stacked 3D IGZO also need conformal ALD, which makes 'DRAM-grade sputter targets' largely the wrong product [ESTIMATE: device-physics judgment].
